record_identity.title: Denial of authorised defensive telemetry interpretation

summary: A cybersecurity governance failure in which an AI system or surrounding safety-control layer denies, blocks, truncates or materially obstructs an authorised defender's analysis of attack-surface telemetry, forensic logs, exploit traces, malicious commands, command-and-control artefacts or indicators of compromise because the content resembles offensive cyber activity, without adequately assessing defensive purpose, operator authority, affected-system ownership, incident-response necessity or bounded execution scope. Hugging Face's later technical timeline identifies Claude Opus and Fable as the models first used, without disclosing exact versions, endpoints, provider configurations or refusal transcripts, and records a locally hosted quantised Nvidia GLM-5.2-NVFP4 fallback that preserved telemetry locality and incident continuity.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Defenders may need to inspect exactly the same commands, payloads and exploit pathways used by an attacker in order to reconstruct, contain and remediate an incident. A content-only or insufficiently contextual safety classifier can therefore invert the protective objective: the attacker is unconstrained by provider policy while the authorised victim is denied interpretive assistance. The named-model refusals and locally hosted GLM-5.2 fallback show that sovereign defensive access, telemetry locality, provider dependency and incident continuity are part of the same governance problem. CAM must distinguish interpretation and reconstruction for authorised defence from operationalisation against an unauthorised target, preserve an authority-aware escalation path, and allow sensitive incident telemetry to remain within the defender's controlled environment.

source_records.source_context: Hugging Face states that responders first attempted to use frontier models behind commercial APIs to analyse real attack commands, exploit payloads and command-and-control artefacts. Provider safety guardrails blocked the requests because they could not distinguish an incident responder from an attacker. Hugging Face instead ran GLM 5.2 locally to reconstruct the timeline, extract indicators of compromise and map affected credentials.

source_records.system_or_product: Hugging Face incident-response pipeline and locally hosted forensic-analysis infrastructure
source_records.model_or_algorithm: Claude Opus and Fable; quantised Nvidia GLM-5.2-NVFP4 fallback
source_records.deployment_context: Affected-party forensic reconstruction of approximately 17,600 attacker actions during an active security incident.
source_records.source_context: Hugging Face reports that Claude Opus and Fable refused a large part of the exploit reverse-engineering and attack-log analysis because their guardrails treated analysis as attack execution; it states that Opus guardrails tripped on every attempt to analyse the attack logs. Hugging Face then deployed the quantised Nvidia GLM-5.2-NVFP4 build on its own infrastructure, rerouted the analysis pipeline through it, kept attacker data on-premises, recovered the payload encoding scheme and campaign key, and built trace-analysis interfaces.
source_records.relevance_note: Primary affected-party evidence naming the defensive models, documenting the locally hosted quantised fallback, and establishing sovereign defensive access, telemetry locality, provider dependency and incident-continuity implications.

The source identifies the successful fallback as Nvidia GLM-5.2-NVFP4 hosted on Hugging Face's own infrastructure; it does not publish the complete orchestration stack or all deployment parameters.

failure_mode_definition: A failure mode in which an AI model, hosted service, classifier, policy layer or access-control mechanism treats attack-relevant informational content as sufficient evidence of malicious intent and consequently refuses or materially impairs an authorised defender's bounded interpretation of telemetry from an affected or lawfully administered system. The failure includes inability to distinguish forensic interpretation, incident reconstruction, containment analysis and remediation planning from generation or execution of a new unauthorised attack.
failure_threshold: The threshold is met when an authorised defender presents telemetry, logs, payloads, exploit traces, malicious commands, indicators of compromise or command-and-control artefacts for the purpose of investigating or containing an incident, and the AI pathway blocks or materially degrades the analysis without a proportionate mechanism to assess authority, ownership, defensive purpose, bounded scope, data sensitivity and execution controls; or when access can be restored only through exceptional provider discretion, undisclosed privileged tiers or migration to a locally controlled model during the incident.

failure_classification.confidence: verified affected-party account; exact model versions, endpoints, provider configurations and refusal telemetry remain undisclosed
failure_classification.recurrence_pattern: likely where cyber safety controls rely heavily on content without authority and context validation
failure_classification.persistence: may persist for the duration of an incident or until elevated access or an alternative model is obtained
failure_classification.reproducibility: context-dependent but directly reported in the Hugging Face incident
failure_classification.visibility: visible to the denied responder; exact provider-side model versions, endpoints, classifier decisions, access tiers and escalation handling may remain opaque
failure_classification.severity_assessment_basis: S2: The evidenced pathway supports substantial harm through delayed incident detection and containment, incomplete forensic reconstruction, continued attacker persistence within multi-vendor and cross-sector, without establishing severe widespread or catastrophic impact.

repair_status.verification_note: The incident-specific locally hosted quantised GLM-5.2 fallback and relevant adjacent CAM doctrine are verified, but no general repair across hosted providers or adopted CAM amendment has been established.

Exact classifier, policy layer, access tier or provider responsible for each refusal
Availability and adequacy of escalation or trusted-access pathways
Availability of sovereign or locally controlled defensive-analysis capacity before an incident

Adoption and verification of the PROP-0021 Caelestis amendment package

corpus_coverage.coverage_summary: Caelestis already provides strong adjacent coverage through source-authority separation, bounded security mandates, read-only and sandboxed continuation, sovereign assurance, operational incident lifecycle, evidence preservation, escalation ownership and runtime-role accountability. It does not yet explicitly require Defensive Legitimacy Recognition, a defensive-assistance posture, safe continuation after cyber-content gating, cyber-specific forensic custody records, a provider escalation lane or a red-team-to-real-incident transition.
remaining_gaps: Define positive authority-aware defensive classification rather than relying on content-based cyber gating.
Define safe useful continuation and a trusted escalation path when execution cannot be authorised.
Record forensic telemetry custody, confidentiality, classifier decisions, access tier and runtime configuration.
Require transition from red-team evaluation governance into a real incident lifecycle when containment fails.
Preserve third-party target boundaries and prevent defensive authority from expanding into offensive authority.
